text:
jess (ACME): Hey, we started getting 401s on SSO logins right after IdP certificate rotation. SAMLResponse rejected with 'signature algorithm mismatch' and RelayState sometimes blank. Can someone help?

maria (support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact error you see in the logs (from the ACS/service) and confirm whether you rotated certs only or also switched signing algorithm?

jess (ACME): Log snippet from our side: ```
2026-03-16T09:12:03Z ERROR saml: assertion validation failed: signature check failed: expected alg=http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#rsa-sha1, got http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmldsig-more#rsa-sha256
status=urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:status:Responder
```

maria (support): That helps. Two common causes: (1) IdP started signing with rsa-sha256 but Redwood's verifier for this tenant is expecting rsa-sha1; or (2) our metadata poller fetched stale metadata because the metadata fetch upstream returned 403/403-like. Can you confirm if ACME's IdP metadata was updated and whether the metadata URL is reachable from our metadata-watcher?

metadata-watcher: automated: last poll attempt for https://idp.acme.example.com/metadata returned 403 at 2026-03-16T09:10:58Z (service account token missing scope: saml.metadata.read).

ida (ACME IdP): We rotated the certs and switched the default signing algorithm to rsa-sha256 as part of the rollout. We also uploaded new metadata to the federation endpoint. I can re-add an rsa-sha1 fallback if needed, but we'd prefer sha256.

sam (eng): Two action paths: A) Quick mitigation: have Ida re-enable rsa-sha1 signing for a short window so signatures match current verifier. B) Root fix: update Redwood tenant metadata and verifier to accept rsa-sha256 signatures (preferred). Before we change verifier behavior, we need the ACME metadata (the XML) showing SignatureMethod and KeyInfo.

maria (support): Jess, can you paste the current metadata.xml (or its signatureMethod lines)? If metadata-watcher returned 403 the platform may still have the old metadata with rsa-sha1 and the IdP is sending rsa-sha256-signed assertions -> signature mismatch.

jess (ACME): Here's the relevant section from the IdP metadata we uploaded last night: ```xml
<ds:Signature>
  <ds:SignedInfo>
    <ds:SignatureMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmldsig-more#rsa-sha256"/>
  </ds:SignedInfo>
</ds:Signature>
<KeyDescriptor use="signing">... new cert ...</KeyDescriptor>
```

maria (support): OK that confirms IdP signs with SHA256 now. The metadata-watcher 403 explains why we still saw old verifier config. The 403 was because the service account token used by our metadata poller lacked the new 'saml.metadata.read' scope after your tenant changes to restrict access. The poller logged: ```
GET https://idp.acme.example.com/metadata -> 403 Forbidden (token missing scope)
X-Request-ID: rw-9a1b2c
```

sam (eng): Root cause summary: IdP changed signing algorithm during rotation (rsa-sha1 -> rsa-sha256) and metadata poll failed due to service account scope change, so Redwood kept old metadata/verifier expecting sha1 -> assertion signature mismatch -> 401. Two independent failures but they combined.

ida (ACME IdP): We can revert signing alg briefly and re-run a controlled rotate. Alternatively, if Redwood can accept sha256 quickly that's fine.

maria (support): Recommended immediate steps (short-term):
- Ida: re-enable rsa-sha1 on IdP for a 10–30m window to restore logins while we update metadata.
- Jess: in Redwood Console -> Auth -> SAML providers -> open ACME provider -> click 'Force refresh metadata' (if present) OR paste metadata XML manually into the tenant settings.
- Ops: grant the metadata poller service account the saml.metadata.read scope so future automatic polls succeed.

sam (eng): Longer-term fixes:
- Add algorithm-flexible signature verifier for tenants: accept both rsa-sha1 and rsa-sha256 if the metadata indicates either; log a high-severity alert when signatureAlgorithm reported in metadata != currently observed algorithm.
- Improve metadata-watcher alerts: surface 403/401 from upstream as a critical tenant-level alert instead of occasional debug trace.
- Add an SLO that flags any SSO tenant with a signature algorithm change during active sessions.

maria (support): For immediate triage, I pushed a manual metadata update for tenant acme-123 with the SHA256 signatureMethod and new cert. Response in logs now shows validation path switched: ```
2026-03-16T09:23:12Z INFO saml: metadata manual upload: validated KeyDescriptor (thumbprint ab:cd:ef)
2026-03-16T09:23:14Z INFO saml: verifier updated for tenant acme-123; accepting rsa-sha256 signatures
```

deploy-bot: deploy: rolling config update to saml-verifier to allow sha256 for tenant acme-123 (canary -> full) started at 2026-03-16T09:26:00Z

maria (support): Can you validate from your side, Jess? Test login for a couple of users and share any remaining error lines.

jess (ACME): Doing a quick smoke now... login succeeded for 2/3 users, one still gets: ```
2026-03-16T09:28:05Z ERROR saml: assertion rejected: AudienceRestriction failed: expected https://app.redwood.example.com/sp, got https://app.redwood.example.com/sp/  (trailing slash)
```

sam (eng): That's a separate normalization issue — trailing slash in Recipient/audience. Quick fix: we can allow a tolerant compare (strip trailing slash) in the verifier for this tenant and then ask ACME to unify their SP config. I'll open a tiny patch to trim trailing slash for audience check for acme-123.

maria (support): TL;DR/resolution checklist:
- metadata-watcher service account: grant saml.metadata.read (ops done?)
- If needed, IdP temporarily enabled sha1 fallback (IdP confirmed reversible)
- Manual metadata upload applied and verifier updated to accept rsa-sha256
- Temporary audience normalization tolerance enabled to avoid trailing-slash 401s
- Follow-ups: improve poller alerts, document 'signature algorithm change' playbook, add unit test for algorithm mapping.

jess (ACME): Thanks — we've re-tested, logins working for all testers after your manual update + audience patch. Please keep me posted when poller scope is fixed so we don't need manual uploads next time. :thumbsup:

maria (support): Will do. I'll create a follow-up ticket to ensure metadata-watcher token scopes are validated nightly and to add the alerting changes Sam suggested. Closing this thread once OP confirms stable for 1 hour.

metadata-watcher: automated: next poll scheduled 2026-03-16T10:00:00Z (will use refreshed token with saml.metadata.read).
